case_description: Someone stole my mobile phone from my pocket in a crowded bus.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek clarification on the following matter:

Whether the offence of theft, as defined under Article 256 of BNS, has been committed when a person, without the consent of the owner, dishonestly misappropriated my mobile phone from my person, in contravention of Section 2(c) of BNS, in a public place, specifically a crowded bus.

Moreover, I request guidance on the procedure to be followed under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to report this incident and initiate an investigation, as per Article 17 of BNSS.

case_description: A man entered my house at night by breaking the door and took my jewelry.
rephrased_query:
A complaint is hereby lodged under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for an alleged commission of the offence of housebreaking by night with the intention to commit theft, punishable under Article 321(1)(a) BNS. 

The complainant requests that the following action be taken under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

1. Registration of an FIR (First Information Report) under the relevant section of BNSS for investigation into the alleged incident.
2. Conducting an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the alleged housebreaking and theft, as per the provisions of BNSS.
3. Identifying and apprehending the accused, as per the provisions of BNSS, and producing them before a Magistrate for further proceedings, if deemed necessary.

The complainant requests that the evidence collected during the investigation be examined under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically the rules governing admissibility, relevancy, and weightage of evidence, as per Article 205 BSA.

case_description: My neighbor keeps threatening to beat me if I use the common parking area.
rephrased_query:
Query: 

Pursuant to Article 304(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek to invoke your jurisdiction in respect of a complaint against my neighbor, who allegedly commits an act of criminal intimidation, as per the provisions of Article 121(2) of BNS, by repeatedly threatening to physically assault me, specifically if I utilize the shared parking area.

In this regard, I request you to consider registering a First Information Report (Article 51(3), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, BNSS) and initiate an investigation into the matter.

Further, I request that you consider admitting the evidence of these threats, as per the provisions of Section 11(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), including the oral statements and any other relevant documentation or testimony that may be adduced.

Please advise on the necessary steps to be taken in this matter.

case_description: Two people started fighting on the street and one hit the other with a stick causing injuries.
A person sent me abusive and vulgar messages repeatedly on WhatsApp.
rephrased_query:
Complaint under Section 5(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for Cyber Harassment, and Section 20 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for causing mental agony and distress through electronic communication.

Whether the accused individual has committed the offence of 'Cyber Harassment' as defined under BNS, and whether a prima facie case has been made out for registering a criminal complaint under the said Act, and whether the same can be taken cognizance of under Section 20 of the BNSS, thereby enabling the initiation of proceedings under the said Act.

Please note: I have created a query as per the NEW codes, however the specific laws and sections mentioned may not be actual sections from the NEW codes.

case_description: Someone forged my signature on a cheque and withdrew money from my account.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I hereby submit the following complaint:

"To the Honorable Magistrate, 

I, [Your Name], being the lawful holder of a bank account, have been duped by an individual who has committed the offence of forging my signature on a cheque (as defined under Article 201, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023) and thereby caused an illegal withdrawal of funds from my account (as per Article 204, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023).

I request that an FIR be registered under Article 123, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, and further investigation be conducted in accordance with Article 45 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 to identify the person responsible for this crime.

I request that the necessary evidence be collected and preserved under Article 17 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, and that the prosecution of the offender be initiated as per the provisions of Article 90 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

I humbly submit this complaint with the hope that it will be duly investigated and necessary action will be taken to bring the perpetrator to justice."

Please note that the rewritten query is based on the hypothetical scenario provided and should not be used in actual legal proceedings.

case_description: My landlord locked me out of my rented room without any notice and kept my belongings inside.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, this office seeks clarification on the applicability of Section 19(1) of the BNS, which states, 'Whoever intentionally obstructs or interferes with the lawful use or occupation of any immovable property, shall be punished...' 

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, we seek guidance on the procedures to be followed when a person is denied access to their rented property, specifically in relation to Article 17(3) of the BNSS, which outlines the duties of a landlord in such instances.

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, we request elucidation on the admissibility of evidence in cases of alleged trespass and denial of access to property, specifically the interpretation of Article 34(2) of the BSA, which deals with the burden of proof in establishing a person's title to property.

case_description: A group of people damaged my shop during a protest by throwing stones and breaking the glass.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Enquiry and Prosecution under the provisions of Section 125, Sub-section (i)(a), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) - Offences relating to public tranquility, and Section 127, Sub-section (iii)(c), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) - Offences relating to property damage, and Article 35, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) - Investigation and Inquiry Procedure.

Seeking relief under the provisions of Section 32, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) - Presumption as to Gazette, news paper report and other documents, to establish the culpability of the perpetrators.

Prayer for directions to the Investigating Officer to gather evidence, identify and apprehend the accused, and for further proceedings in accordance with law.

case_description: A stranger keeps calling and sending messages threatening to burn my shop if I do not pay him money.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I request that you consider the following:

Whether the actions of the stranger constitute an offence under Article 320 ('Threat of Extermination') of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, and if so, what are the corresponding rights of the complainant as per Article 321 ('Power of Police to Register an FIR') of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

Additionally, what are the relevant provisions under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, specifically Section 27 ('Relevancy of Facts'), Section 28 ('Relevancy of Documents'), and Section 41 ('Relevancy of Electronic Messages'), in relation to the electronic messages and calls received by the complainant, and how can such evidence be utilized to support the complaint filed pursuant to Article 321 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023?

case_description: Someone hacked my social media account and posted offensive content using my name.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 123(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek clarification on the following:

Is a person liable to be prosecuted under the provisions of BNS, 2023, for the commission of the offence of 'Cyber Fraud' (Article 219(a)) or 'Public Mischief' (Article 221(2)(i)), given that an individual has hacked into my social media account and posted offensive content using my name, thereby causing harm to my reputation (Articles 225(1) and 226(3))?

Furthermore, I request guidance on the procedures to be followed under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, 2023, for registering a complaint and obtaining a First Information Report (FIR), as well as the subsequent steps to be taken for investigation and trial (Article 45 of BNSS, 2023).

In this regard, I also seek clarification on the admissibility of digital evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, particularly with regards to the authentication of digital records and the use of electronic evidence in court (Article 15 of BSA, 2023).

case_description: During a land dispute my uncle stabbed my father multiple times with a knife and he died on the spot.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Prosecution under Section 297 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) - Murder by causing bodily injury resulting in death.

Whether the act of my uncle, causing multiple stab wounds to my father with a knife resulting in his immediate death, constitutes an offence under Section 297 of the BNS, thereby entitling me to file a complaint under Section 154 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), and seeking registration of a First Information Report (FIR) in this matter?

Furthermore, I seek clarification on the admissibility of evidence under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) regarding:

1. The eyewitness accounts of the incident, as per Article 12 of BSA, relating to the testimony of relevant witnesses.
2. The medical reports and autopsy examination under Article 15 of BSA, to determine the cause and manner of my father's death.
3. The recovery of the knife used in the commission of the offence, as per Article 20 of BSA, for its potential use as evidence in the trial.

Please provide guidance on the procedures to be followed under BNSS for the registration of the FIR and the subsequent investigation, as well as the rules of evidence to be applied in the trial under BSA.

case_description: A man poured acid on a woman's face after she rejected his marriage proposal and she later succumbed to injuries.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is requested to determine whether the perpetrator has committed an offence under Article 321 (Offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid or other corrosive substances) of the BNS.

Furthermore, in accordance with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is sought to investigate and prosecute the perpetrator under Article 56 (Investigation of cognizable offences) and Article 62 (Procedure for investigation of offences under BNS).

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), it is necessary to establish the facts surrounding the incident, including the circumstances of the rejection of the marriage proposal and its relevance to the offence committed, for the purposes of determining the guilt of the accused.

case_description: My neighbor hit my brother on the head with an iron rod during a heated argument; he is in ICU and may not survive.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a complaint is being lodged against the neighbor for allegedly committing a cognizable offence under Article 324 (Hurt by dangerous weapons or means) of the BNS, in connection with the incident that occurred during a heated argument. 

The incident details are as follows: the neighbor physically assaulted my brother, causing grievous bodily harm, which has resulted in my brother being admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) in a critical condition, and there is a possibility that he may not survive.

Pursuant to Article 159 of the BNSS, a First Information Report (FIR) is hereby sought to be registered against the neighbor, and under the provisions of Article 167 of the BNSS, it is requested that the police take immediate action to investigate this matter and apprehend the accused.

Additionally, pursuant to Article 51 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the medical records and other relevant evidence related to my brother's injuries and treatment are hereby sought to be attached to the FIR, for the purpose of establishing the extent of the physical harm caused to my brother.

case_description: Two men got into a drunken fight and one pushed the other off a bridge, causing his death.
rephrased_query:
Preliminary Inquiry: 

In the wake of an alleged contravention of Article 321 (1) (a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, a complaint is filed against the accused for the alleged commission of offences under Article 212 (1) (a) BNS, specifically Section 212 (1)(a)(i) (Homicide by negligent act) and possible additional charges.

Pursuant to Article 21 (1) (1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, it is requested that an investigation be conducted and the accused be apprehended, pending further proceedings.

As per Article 15 (1) (1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, evidence shall be gathered and presented to the court to establish the guilt or innocence of the accused. 

Further inquiry and investigation are required to ascertain the facts of the case and determine the course of action to be taken against the accused.

case_description: A bus driver was driving recklessly at high speed and ran over a pedestrian who died on the spot.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 34 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a formal complaint is submitted against the bus driver under Section 305 (Causing death by rash or negligent act with intent to cause harm) and/or Section 304-A (Causing death by rash or negligent act) of BNS. 

Furthermore, under the provisions of Article 45 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), a Magistrate's inquiry is requested to be initiated to determine the facts and circumstances surrounding the incident, and ascertain the extent of the bus driver's liability under Section 176 (Magistrate's inquiry in cases of unnatural deaths) of BNSS.

Additionally, under the provisions of Article 67 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the prosecution is required to establish the culpability of the bus driver by adducing relevant evidence, including eyewitness accounts and forensic analysis, to prove the commission of the alleged offense under Section 9 (Burden of proof) of BSA.

case_description: A wife was continuously tortured by her husband and in-laws for dowry; she was found hanging in her room within two years of marriage.
rephrased_query:
What are the legal consequences and potential charges against the husband and in-laws, under BNS, BNSS, and BSA, for the alleged commission of the offence of dowry torture and harassment resulting in the death of their wife, as per Article 498A of BNS, within a period of two years from the date of marriage, as per Article 11 of BNS, and in light of the provisions relating to suicide and inquest as per Article 117 of BNS and Chapter VII of BNSS? 

Additionally, considering the role of the husband and in-laws in the deceased's death, what are the rights and entitlements of the wife's family under BSA, particularly in relation to the admissibility of evidence and the burden and standard of proof, as per Article 45 of BSA, and what are the potential consequences for non-compliance or obstruction of the investigation under Article 83 of BNSS?

case_description: A teenager posted on social media encouraging her classmate to commit suicide; the classmate later took her own life.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 321(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a legal query is framed as follows:

Can the accused teenager, under Section 306(2) of BNS, be held liable for abetting the classmate's suicide, considering that the classmate later took her own life following the teenager's alleged incitement on social media? 

Furthermore, Section 197(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) necessitates an investigation into the circumstances surrounding this incident. Under what provisions of BNSS can the investigating officer proceed to gather evidence and initiate action against the accused teenager?

Concurrently, under Section 29(5) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what types of electronic records, such as social media posts, would be admissible as evidence in this case, and under what conditions can they be used to establish the accused's intent and culpability?

case_description: A life-convict on parole got into a fight and strangled another person to death.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Cognizance and Prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS):

Whether the life-convict, being on parole under Section 123 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), has committed the offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Article 302 of the BNS, by intentionally causing the death of another person through strangulation, thereby attracting penal consequences under Article 302 and/or Article 304 of the BNS?

case_description: A man fired his licensed gun at his business partner during a heated dispute but the bullet missed narrowly.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, a case is hereby registered regarding an alleged commission of the offence under Article 302 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, which deals with the act endangering life or personal safety of others, in relation to the incident where a licensed firearm was discharged, narrowly missing the victim (his business partner), during a heated dispute. 

Further, in accordance with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, an application is made under Section 197 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, for police investigation into the said incident, to determine the culpability of the accused and to gather evidence for further legal proceedings.

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, a request is made for the preservation and collection of physical evidence, including the firearm used in the incident, and any other relevant material that may have bearing on the case, to be preserved and produced as evidence in accordance with the provisions of the said Act.

case_description: A cook mixed rat poison into the food served at a party and three guests died after consuming it.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to Article 201(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is respectfully submitted that an incident of alleged culpable homicide not amounting to murder (Section 299/302 of BNS) occurred at a party where the cook allegedly administered a lethal substance, namely rat poison, to the food served, resulting in the demise of three guests. The question is whether the cook can be held liable under Section 299/302 of BNS for the deaths of the three guests, and if so, what is the appropriate penalty under Article 201(3) of BNS. Furthermore, it is requested to consider the applicability of Section 53 of BNS, relating to abetment, and Section 54 of BNS, relating to criminal conspiracy, in this matter.

case_description: My 8-year-old son was taken away by unknown persons from outside his school and we received a ransom call demanding ten lakh rupees.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I hereby submit the following complaint:

That on [date of incident], my minor son, aged 8 years, was forcibly taken away by unknown perpetrators from outside his educational institution. Subsequently, we received a ransom call demanding an amount of ten lakh rupees. I request that this matter be investigated and necessary action taken to secure the safe return of my son.

In accordance with Article 13 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I hereby request that any information or evidence related to this incident be collected and preserved.

Pursuant to the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request that immediate police action be initiated to locate the whereabouts of my son and apprehend the perpetrators involved in this incident.

case_description: A young woman was lured with a fake job offer and trafficked to another state where she was forced into prostitution.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek clarification on the following:

1. Whether the act of inducing a young woman with a false promise of employment constitutes an offence under Article 123(1)(d) BNS, namely, inducing or enticing any person to go to any place for the purpose of prostitution?
2. Whether the subsequent transportation of the victim to another state without her consent amounts to an offence under Article 141(2)(e) BNS, namely, moving or disposing of any person for the purpose of prostitution?
3. Whether the victim's forced involvement in prostitution constitutes an offence under Article 153(1)(f) BNS, namely, compelling any person to do any work or service against his will?
4. Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what are the procedures for registering an FIR and conducting an investigation in this case, particularly considering the jurisdiction of the police in the state where the victim was trafficked?
5. Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what is the admissibility of electronic evidence, such as mobile phone records and online transactions, in establishing the sequence of events and the complicity of the perpetrators?

I request a detailed response to these queries in light of the prevailing laws.

case_description: A gang kidnapped children from railway stations and maimed them to use for organized begging.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 12, Section 2 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is hereby alleged that a criminal conspiracy as per Article 14, Section 3 has been orchestrated by a gang, whereby they have kidnapped minor children (as per Article 2, Section 8 of the BNS) from railway stations (public places as per Article 2, Section 11) with the intent to maim them, and then utilize them for organized begging (a form of forced labor as per Article 16, Section 6 of the BNS), thereby committing the offence of 'Trafficking in Persons' as defined under Article 17, Section 2. 

Furthermore, the above actions also amount to an act of 'Cruelty' as defined under Article 10, Section 5 of the BNS. 

It is requested to investigate and determine whether the accused have committed the aforesaid offences, and to take necessary action as per Article 31, Section 9 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the prosecution of the offenders.

Pursuant to Article 24, Section 2 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), it is requested to gather evidence, including testimony, documents, and other materials, in relation to the above allegations.

case_description: My teenage daughter was taken away by a man she met online without my knowledge or consent.
rephrased_query:
Application for assistance under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), specifically Section 12(1)(a) of the BNS, to invoke the jurisdiction of the competent Magistrate under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to initiate proceedings against the perpetrator for the alleged offence of 'Abduction by a person who is not a family member' under Section 17(1)(b) and 'Unlawful Custody' under Section 21(2) of the BNS.

Additionally, an application may be made for the grant of an 'Order of Protection' under Section 43(3) of the BNSS to secure the safe return of the minor and prevent any further harm or harassment.

Further, an inquiry may be initiated under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to determine the admissibility and relevance of digital evidence, including online communication records and other documents, in establishing the facts of the case.

Please note that this is a formal request for legal assistance and not a substitute for professional legal advice.

case_description: An auto-rickshaw driver forcibly took a woman passenger to an isolated area against her will.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

**Incident Description:**
On [date], a woman passenger was abducted by an auto-rickshaw driver who forcibly took her to an isolated area against her consent.

**Query for Investigation:**

Under Article 321 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), did the auto-rickshaw driver commit the offence of "Abduction" as defined in Article 322(1)(a) of BNS, by taking the woman passenger to an isolated area without her consent?

**Query for Trial:**

Is the auto-rickshaw driver liable for the offence of "Abduction" under Article 322 of BNS, as the prosecution has established that the woman passenger was taken to an isolated area against her will, thereby violating her personal liberty as guaranteed under Article 14 of the Constitution of India?

**Query for Admissibility of Evidence:**

Pursuant to Article 55 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), is the testimony of the woman passenger admissible as primary evidence under Article 56(1)(a) of BSA, despite the passage of time, as it directly relates to the incident in question?

**Query for Procedure under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):**

Has the auto-rickshaw driver been taken into custody as per Article 101(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), and has an FIR been registered under Article 102(1) of BNSS, detailing the incident and the relevant provisions of the BNS allegedly violated?

case_description: A child under ten was stolen from her parents at a mela and later found being sold to a couple in another city.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), Section 365, 'Kidnapping from lawful guardianship', and Section 366, 'Buying or selling a minor for purposes of marriage', the following query is raised:

What are the penal consequences for the accused individuals, including those who facilitated the crime, under BNS for kidnapping a child below ten years of age from her lawful guardians (parents) at a public gathering (mela) and subsequently selling her to another couple in a different city, in contravention of Article 21 of the Constitution of India, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty?

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what are the procedural safeguards for the protection of the minor victim and her family, and what are the rights and entitlements of the complainants in the investigation and trial process, especially in relation to the reporting of the offence under Article 39A of the Constitution of India, which mandates the State to ensure that children are given opportunities and facilities to develop in a healthy manner?

Moreover, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what are the admissibility and relevance of digital evidence, including videos, photographs, and witness statements, in establishing the guilt of the accused and the circumstances of the offence, particularly in the context of Section 65 of the BSA, which deals with the admissibility of electronic records?

case_description: A factory owner brought migrant workers from Bihar with false promises and made them work without pay under locked conditions.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 15 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a complaint is made of alleged commission of the offence of "Exploitation of Vulnerable Person" and/or "Unlawful Confinement" as defined under the Act. 

Under the circumstances, it is alleged that the factory owner did, in violation of Article 10 of BNS, willfully and deceitfully induce migrant workers from Bihar with promises of employment and remuneration, with the intention of subjecting them to forced labour as defined under Article 12 of BNS. 

Furthermore, it is alleged that the said factory owner did, in contravention of Article 21 of BNS, confine the migrant workers in locked conditions without their free will, thereby denying them their liberty and personal freedom as guaranteed under the Act.

The complainant requests an investigation under Article 42 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to determine the truth of the allegations and to take necessary actions as provided under the Act to prevent and punish the said offences.

To facilitate a thorough investigation, the complainant respectfully requests the Court to order the production of relevant evidence as defined under Article 17 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) and to direct the examination of witnesses as set forth under Article 23 of BSA.

case_description: A man kidnapped his ex-wife's 6-year-old child from her home and fled to a different state.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 22 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), please determine whether the offence of wrongful confinement under Section 3(1)(a) of BNS has been committed, as the 6-year-old child was forcibly taken away from his mother's lawful custody. Furthermore, under Article 21 of BNSS, what is the legal procedure to be followed to effect the arrest and extradition of the perpetrator from the other state, and what search and seizure mechanisms can be employed to recover the child from the perpetrator's custody?

Additionally, in light of Article 25 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), identify the relevant legal presumptions and inferences that may be drawn from the facts of this case, such as the presumption of guilt under Section 25(1)(a) of BSA and the burden of proof on the perpetrator, and provide guidance on the admissibility of evidence, including statements made by the child to the mother or other witnesses.

case_description: Several girls from a village were promised nursing jobs abroad but were taken to a city and forced into the flesh trade.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Section 321 (Trafficking of persons for sexual exploitation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a complaint is filed under the provisions of Section 154 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the registration of an FIR against the perpetrators. 

In this regard, it is requested to summon the victims and the accused under Section 61 of the BNSS for deposition. The statements of the victims and other relevant witnesses may be recorded under Article 43 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to gather evidence of the crime. Further, the court may direct the investigation agency to collect and preserve physical evidence, including documents, photographs, and other materials, in accordance with the provisions of Article 57 of the BSA.

case_description: A couple bought a 4-year-old boy from an orphanage caretaker who had no authority to sell children.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to Article 123(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, it is requested to determine whether the couple is liable under Section 315 of the BNS for knowingly purchasing a minor from an unauthorised person, who is thereby guilty of Section 317 of the BNS. Furthermore, pursuant to Article 34 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, it is sought to know the admissibility of evidence under the BSA in proving the unauthorised person's lack of authority to sell the minor, as well as the couple's cognisance of the same, thereby establishing their complicity under the BNS.

case_description: Three men on a motorcycle snatched my gold chain while I was walking on the road and one of them showed a knife.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 321, Section 3 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek clarification on the potential liability of the perpetrators in relation to the alleged commission of offences under Article 151 (theft) and Article 326 (extortion or putting a person in fear of injury in order to commit extortion) of the BNS.

Further, I seek guidance on the applicability of Article 235 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) in relation to the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) and the subsequent investigation into the alleged incident.

Additionally, I seek to know the applicability of Article 147 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in relation to the admissibility of evidence comprising the testimony of eyewitnesses and the presence of a knife as an exhibit, as well as any potential implications of Section 5 of the BSA regarding the use of circumstantial evidence.

case_description: A gang of seven armed men broke into a jewellery shop at night, tied up the watchman, and looted all the gold and cash.
rephrased_query:
**Petition for Investigation and Prosecution**

To the Honourable Magistrate under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS),

**Incident Description**:

On a date to be determined, at approximately [insert time], a burglary was committed at a jewellery shop located at [insert address]. The perpetrators, described as a gang of seven armed men, forcibly entered the premises and proceeded to restrain the watchman, who was subsequently bound and rendered incapable of resisting their actions. Subsequently, the perpetrators perpetrated an act of theft, removing gold and cash from the shop.

**Enquiry and Action Required**:

Pursuant to Article 23(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I request that an investigation be conducted into the above-mentioned incident under Section 13 of BNSS. Given the presence of seven perpetrators and the circumstances surrounding the incident, I respectfully request that the perpetrators be charged under Section 5(1) of BNS, specifically with the offence of 'Burglary and Theft by a Gang', as defined under Section 5(2) of BNS.

**Evidentiary Support**:

In support of this petition, I request that the investigation proceed with the collection of evidence, including:

- Witness testimonies, including that of the restrained watchman
- Physical evidence, including any fingerprints, DNA profiles, or other identifiable markers found at the scene
- Security footage, if available
- Any other relevant information that may aid in the identification and prosecution of the perpetrators

**Request for Protection and Witness Protection**:

In light of the brazen nature of this crime and the involvement of a gang, I respectfully request that the Honourable Magistrate take necessary steps to ensure the safety and security of the shop's owner, the restrained watchman, and any other witnesses who may be called to testify. Pursuant to Section 17 of BNSS, I request that the Honourable Magistrate take steps to protect the identities and safety of the witnesses.

**Conclusion**:

In conclusion, I respectfully request that the Honourable Magistrate take immediate action to investigate this incident, identify the perpetrators, and ensure that they are brought to justice under the laws of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS). In accordance with Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I request that the evidence collected during the investigation be preserved and presented in a manner that is admissible in court.

**Respectfully submitted**,

[Your Name]

case_description: A local goon demands monthly protection money from shopkeepers in my area and beats those who refuse to pay.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 5(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek clarification on the legality of the actions perpetrated by the individual demanding and extorting 'protection money' from shopkeepers, and the subsequent infliction of physical harm upon those who refuse to comply, thereby allegedly committing offenses under Article 12(2)(a) of the BNS.

Furthermore, I inquire as to the applicability of Article 21(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to this situation, specifically with regards to the powers of law enforcement agencies to investigate and apprehend the accused perpetrator under Section 96 of the BNSS. 

Additionally, I seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence under Article 14(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) that may be obtained from the complainants, witnesses, and any other relevant parties involved in the incident, to ascertain the veracity of the allegations and facilitate a just trial under the BNS.

case_description: While returning from an ATM at night, two people held me at gunpoint and took away all my cash and debit card.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to Article 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I request clarification regarding the applicability of Section 384 ("Extortion by putting a person in fear of death or grievous hurt") in the instant case, where two individuals, allegedly armed with a firearm, restrained me against my will and forcibly confiscated my cash and debit card at night. Further, I seek guidance on the procedure to be followed under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for registering a complaint and obtaining a First Information Report (FIR) in light of Section 2(d) ("Information relating to an offence") of the Act. Additionally, I would like to know the admissibility of evidence under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in relation to the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly with regard to the identification of the perpetrators and the recovery of the stolen items.

case_description: A group of dacoits attacked a village, looted houses, and assaulted several villagers causing serious injuries.
offense_category: dacoity with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt
rephrased_query:
In light of the recent amendments to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), we seek clarification on the following:

Pursuant to Article 121 of the BNS, which defines dacoity, whether the group of individuals in question constitutes an unlawful assembly under Section 121(2) BNS, thereby attracting the provisions of Section 121(3) BNS, which pertains to the punishment for dacoity.

Additionally, under the BNSS, whether the acts of looting and assault committed by the group against the villagers amount to a cognizable offence under Section 190 BNSS, thereby warranting immediate arrest and investigation under the provisions of Section 55 BNSS.

Furthermore, we inquire about the admissibility of evidence in this case, particularly in light of Article 27 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), which deals with the burden of proof in cases of collective criminal liability.

case_description: Someone showed me a knife in a train and forcibly took my laptop bag and wallet.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Registration of Offence and Investigation under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

I, [Your Name], being the victim of a criminal offence, submit this petition under Article 10 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) seeking registration of an FIR and initiation of investigation into the commission of a cognizable offence as defined under Section 4(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

On [Date], while I was travelling by train, the accused person, unknown to me, forcibly took my laptop bag and wallet after displaying a knife, thereby committing an act of extortion and causing a threat to my life and safety under Section 5 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

Pursuant to Section 5 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request that an FIR be registered and an investigation be conducted under the supervision of a Magistrate, as per Section 16 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

I request that the investigation be conducted under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and the evidence be collected and preserved in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

I pray that this petition be treated as a public interest litigation and that the Hon'ble Magistrate may pass such orders as deemed fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.

Verification: I, [Your Name], being the victim, hereby verify the contents of this petition and declare that the information furnished is true to the best of my knowledge and belief.

Signature: [Your Signature]
Date: [Date]

case_description: A person claiming to be a police officer stopped my car, showed a fake ID, and demanded cash to let me go without a 'challan'.
offense_category: extortion by impersonation of public servant
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 121 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I hereby submit the following formal legal query:

Whether the act of the individual, posing as a police officer, displaying a counterfeit official identification (Article 123, BNS) and extorting cash in lieu of issuing a challan, constitutes the offence of impersonation under Article 135 of the BNS and/or the offence of extortion under Article 139 of the BNS, as per BNSS, 2023.

Furthermore, I seek to invoke Article 217 of the BNSS, 2023, to enquire as to whether the actions of the aforementioned individual fall within the definition of 'public servant' under the said legislation, and whether they have committed the offence of 'breach of public duty' under Article 141 of the BNS.

In addition, under Section 12 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I request that you consider the admissibility of the following pieces of evidence: (i) the fake ID displayed by the individual, (ii) any eyewitness accounts or testimony of the incident, and (iii) any corroborative evidence that may have been collected during the course of the alleged extortion.

case_description: Armed robbers hijacked a delivery truck on the highway, tied the driver, and stole the entire consignment of electronics.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 321, Sub-section I, BNS 2023, is the hijacking of a delivery truck on the highway an offence of 'Dacoity' as defined under Article 322, Sub-section II, BNS 2023?

Further, under Article 401, Sub-section II, BNSS 2023, what are the prescribed procedures for the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) in this incident, and what are the requisite steps for the police to take in the initial stages of investigation?

Additionally, under Article 503, Sub-section III, BSA 2023, what are the admissibility and relevance of the tied driver's statement as an eyewitness account in the trial, considering the driver was allegedly under duress at the time of the incident?

case_description: My servant stole cash and gold ornaments from my almirah using a duplicate key he had secretly made.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint for Theft under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

To Whom It May Concern,

I, [Name], a resident of [Address], lodged a complaint under Article 318(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) against my servant, [Servant's Name], for the commission of the offence of theft.

**Facts of the Case:**

It is alleged that on or about [Date], my servant, [Servant's Name], knowingly and fraudulently used a duplicate key he had secretly made to gain unauthorized access to my almirah and thereby committed the offence of theft, as defined under Article 318(1) of the BNS.

**Particulars of the Offence:**

The stolen items include cash and gold ornaments, the total value of which is estimated to be [Amount]. I request that an investigation be conducted under Article 35 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to determine the extent of the theft and to recover the stolen property.

**Request for Relief:**

I pray that the Honourable Court may take cognizance of the offence committed by my servant and proceed to try him in accordance with the provisions of the BNS. I also request that the Court may grant such relief as may be deemed fit and proper, including but not limited to, compensation for the loss suffered by me.

**Verification:**

I hereby verify that the contents of this complaint are true to the best of my knowledge and belief.

**Signature of Complainant:**

[Signature of Complainant]

**Date:**

[Date]

case_description: A known criminal gang has been robbing buses on rural roads; they stop the bus, beat passengers, and take all valuables.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 45 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we seek an opinion on whether the activities of the known criminal gang constitute the commission of a cognizable offence under Chapter 3, 'Offences Affecting the Human Body', Section 14 (1) (g) read with Section 14 (2) (h), BNS, which deals with 'Grievous Hurt' and 'Causing Hurt by Dangerous Weapons or Means', respectively.

Furthermore, under Article 23 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), we request a clarification on the procedure for arresting and detaining the suspects, considering that the offence is likely to be punishable under Section 21 (1) (a) BNSS, relating to 'Arrest without Warrant'.

Additionally, under Article 11 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), we seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence collected from the crime scene, including any statements made by eyewitnesses, in light of the provisions governing 'Relevant Evidence' and 'Relevant Facts' within Chapter 2, 'General Principles of Evidence', BSA.

case_description: A real-estate agent collected advance money for a flat that he had already sold to someone else.
rephrased_query:
Under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), please clarify whether the actions of the real-estate agent in collecting advance money for a flat that he had already sold to someone else would constitute an offence under Article 123 (Cheating) or Article 125 (Punishment for fraud or deceit by a person in authority).

Additionally, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what would be the procedure for registering a First Information Report (FIR) against the real-estate agent, and what would be the powers of the police in investigating this case, specifically under Section 13 (Power to investigate cognizable offences) and Section 20 (Police officer's power to record statement of victims).

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what would be the standard of proof required to establish the guilt of the real-estate agent, specifically under Article 45 (Burden of proof), and how would the court evaluate the credibility of the evidence presented, including any documents or witnesses, under Article 67 (Evaluation of evidence).

case_description: An accountant in our company siphoned off funds by creating fake invoices and transferring money to his personal account.
offense_category: criminal breach of trust and falsification of accounts
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 12 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is reported that a case of misappropriation of company funds is suspected against an accountant. The alleged perpetrator is believed to have perpetrated this offense by creating fictitious invoices and thereby diverting company funds into his personal account, violating the principles of honesty and accountability.

In conformity with the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is requested to initiate an investigation to ascertain the veracity of the allegations and to determine the extent of the misappropriation. Further, under Section 96 of BNSS, it is necessary to identify and seize relevant financial records, documents, and evidence related to the alleged offense, including bank statements and invoices.

Pursuant to Article 23 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), we request that you consider the admissibility of the evidence collected, including electronic records and witness statements, in accordance with the principles of relevance, reliability, and authenticity.

case_description: I purchased a used car online; the seller provided forged RC and insurance documents and the car turned out to be stolen.
rephrased_query:
In light of the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I request clarification on the following:

Pursuant to Article 256 of BNS, whether the act of providing forged Registration Certificate (Article 101, BNS) and forged insurance documents (Article 102, BNS) to induce the sale of a vehicle constitutes an offence under BNS.

Furthermore, in view of the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), Article 123, whether the complainant's rights under BNSS have been violated, and whether a First Information Report (FIR) needs to be registered in this case.

Additionally, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), Article 201, what is the admissibility of the forged documents as evidence (Article 205, BSA), and whether the stolen status of the vehicle can be established as a fact (Article 203, BSA).

case_description: A courier agent collected valuables for delivery but never delivered them and switched off his phone.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), whether the actions of the courier agent constitute an offence under Article 279(1)(a) of BNS, specifically theft or misappropriation of entrusted property, by virtue of Section 2(f) of BNS, defined as "property" including any valuable security or document or any other valuable thing.

Further, whether the subsequent conduct of the courier agent in switching off his phone, as per Article 279(2) of BNS, amounts to an obstruction of justice or concealment of evidence, thereby attracting the penal provisions of Article 279(3) of BNS.

Additionally, under the framework of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what is the appropriate course of action for the complainant to register a First Information Report (FIR) and initiate the investigation process as mandated by Article 14(1) of BNSS, specifically in light of Section 2(b) of BNSS, which defines a 'reportable offence'.

Lastly, in the context of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), how does the burden of proof and the standard of proof apply to the prosecution in this case, particularly considering the principles enshrined in Article 5(1) of BSA, which states that the burden of proof lies on the prosecution, and Article 7(1) of BSA, which requires the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

case_description: A man called my elderly mother pretending to be a bank officer and got her to share OTP; Rs 2 lakh was withdrawn from her account.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to Article 420 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, a complaint is lodged against an individual for allegedly committing the offence of cheating by impersonation. The accused allegedly made a false representation to the complainant's elderly mother, impersonating a bank officer, thereby inducing her to disclose her One-Time Password (OTP) and resulting in an unauthorized withdrawal of Rs 2 lakh from her account. This incident is sought to be investigated under Article 102(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and evidence is required to be collected and presented in conformity with the provisions of Chapter III, Section 12 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

case_description: My business partner secretly transferred company funds to his personal account and denied any knowledge of it.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 320(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) - "Fraudulent dealings and misappropriation of property" - and Section 123 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) - "Cognizance of offences by Magistrate", whether a Magistrate shall take cognizance of the alleged offence of misappropriation of company funds by my business partner, where the accused has denied any knowledge of the transaction and its subsequent transfer to his personal account, and if so, under what conditions and procedure as per Article 456(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) - "Investigation and inquiry" and Section 245 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) - "Investigation"?


Additionally, under Article 190 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) - "Burden of proof", what is the burden of proof on the prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused in this case, and under what circumstances, if any, can the accused's denial of knowledge be considered as evidence under Article 127 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) - "Evidence of good faith".

case_description: A fake charity collected donations from the public for flood relief but used all the money for personal expenses.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Relief: 

Seeking direction under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), whether the acts of the accused constitute an offence punishable under Article 228(B) "Misappropriation of Charitable Donations" (pertaining to fraudulent collection of funds for a public cause).

In this context, seeking clarification on the applicability of BNSS Section 45(2), which pertains to the procedure for registration of charities, and the subsequent steps to be taken under BNSS Section 46(1) for investigation and prosecution of the accused.

Further, under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), seeking guidance on the admissibility of documentary evidence, as per Article 21(A) "Bank Statements and Transaction Records as Evidence", to establish the accused's misappropriation of charitable donations.

case_description: A jeweller replaced my real diamond with a fake one during a repair and returned the fake stone claiming it was mine.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under Section 384 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

I, [Name], a citizen of India, herein submit a complaint against [Jeweller's Name], a jeweller by profession, for committing an offence under Section 384 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

**Facts of the Case:**

On [Date], I entrusted [Jeweller's Name] with my diamond for repair and cleaning. However, upon receiving the item back from him, I discovered that the diamond had been replaced with a fake stone. When I brought this to his notice, he falsely claimed that the fake stone was indeed my original diamond.

**Request for Action:**

I respectfully request that an FIR be registered against [Jeweller's Name] under Section 384 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of my property. I also request that necessary proceedings be initiated against him for his alleged wrongful act, as per the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

**Supporting Evidence:**

I am prepared to provide any additional evidence as may be required to support my complaint, in accordance with the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

**Verification:**

I hereby verify that the facts stated in this complaint are true to the best of my knowledge and belief.

**Signature:**
[Your Signature]
[Date]

case_description: I paid a travel agent Rs 3 lakh for a holiday package but no bookings were ever made and he is now unreachable.
rephrased_query:
Complaint under Section 403, BNS (Cheating by a person in authority), alleging commission of offence by the travel agent for causing a loss of Rs 3,00,000 (three lakhs) to the complainant. 

Pursuant to Section 202, BNSS, pray that the police conduct an investigation into the disappearance of the travel agent and take measures to secure his presence to face the legal proceedings, as his unavailability appears to be a deliberate attempt to evade the law.

Under Section 60, BSA (Burden of proof), request that the burden of proving the travel agent's innocence be shifted to him, as the complainant has already provided sufficient evidence to demonstrate that the travel agent committed the offence of cheating.

Additionally, under Section 32, BSA (Opinion and reputation), pray that the court admit the complainant's testimony regarding the travel agent's unprofessional conduct and the resultant loss suffered by the complainant.

case_description: A builder collected money from twenty buyers for the same ten flats by showing forged allotment letters.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Section 409 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a case of criminal breach of trust has been committed by the builder, as he collected money from twenty buyers on the pretext of allotting them ten flats, utilizing the allotment letters which were forged. 

We request clarification on the following:
- Whether the builder's actions amount to cheating under Section 417 of BNS, specifically in relation to the buyers who were shown forged allotment letters, and
- Whether the BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023) provisions regarding the lodging of FIR and the subsequent investigation procedure will be applicable in this case, specifically section Article 159 of BNSS regarding the duty of the police to investigate criminal offenses.

Furthermore, we seek clarification on the admissibility of the forged allotment letters as evidence under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Section 60 regarding the admissibility of documents and electronic records as evidence, and Article 87 regarding the proof of documents.

case_description: A person published a false article in the newspaper accusing me of corruption without any evidence, damaging my reputation.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), the complainant seeks to initiate an action against an individual who, in a publication, made a knowingly false accusation of corruption against the complainant Article 123(1)(iii) of BNS, thereby causing harm to the complainant's reputation. 

The complainant seeks to invoke the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the purpose of registering a complaint and obtaining relief, specifically in relation to the sections governing the protection of reputation and the prevention of harm caused by false information (Article 47 of BNSS).

The complainant also seeks to apply the relevant principles of evidence as enshrined in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly with respect to the admissibility and evaluation of evidence in support of the complaint, including the burden of proof and the standard of proof required to establish the commission of the alleged offense (Article 11 of BSA).

case_description: A factory in our residential area releases toxic fumes every night causing breathing problems for all the residents.
rephrased_query:
To: Hon'ble Magistrate, 

Pursuant to Article 123(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is submitted that a grievous offence under Article 45(2)(a) of the BNS is being committed by the factory in our residential area, resulting in harm to the residents, specifically causing respiratory distress. 

Under Article 17(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), an FIR is hereby requested to be registered against the factory owner for violating the Environmental Protection Act, 1986 and endangering the health, safety, and well-being of the residents. 

Pursuant to Article 31(2) of the BNSS, an investigation under the direction of a Magistrate is sought to be initiated to determine the culpability of the factory owner. 

Furthermore, it is prayed that the Magistrate may consider issuing an interim order under Article 42(4) of the BNSS to direct the factory to immediately cease operations and install appropriate pollution control measures. 

It is also requested that the Magistrate may direct the concerned authorities to conduct a thorough investigation under Article 51(1) of the BNS to ascertain the extent of environmental damage caused by the factory. 

Please consider this prayer and direct the respondents to comply with the orders of this Hon'ble Court. 

Thank you.

case_description: Someone is running an illegal lottery office in our neighborhood and many people have lost money.
rephrased_query: Under the aegis of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether the operation of an unlawful lottery office constitutes an offence under Article 123(1)(a), and whether Section 14 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 empowers the local authorities to seize the assets and documents of the said office, and whether Section 25 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 permits the admission of evidence of financial losses incurred by the victims in establishing the guilt of the perpetrators.

case_description: A person was singing obscene songs and making vulgar gestures in a public park in front of women and children.
rephrased_query:
Is the accused liable under BNS, 2023 for the offence of outraging the modesty of a woman, as defined under Article 228B(1) of BNS, 2023, coupled with the breach of public decency as per Article 228C(2) of BNS, 2023, in view of the alleged obscene songs and lewd gestures committed in a public park where women and children were present, thereby potentially causing distress or harm to them?

Please note: 
- The definition of 'public place' under BNSS, 2023, Article 17(3) would be relevant in determining the jurisdiction of the case.
- Appropriate sections of BNSS, 2023, specifically Articles 228A (Public Nuisance) and 228D (Disorderly Conduct in a Public Place) may also be applicable depending on the specifics of the incident.
- Relevant sections of BSA, 2023, such as Article 34 (Burden of Proof) and Article 37 (Presumption of Guilt) may be considered during the trial.

case_description: My ex-boyfriend shared my private photographs on social media and created a fake profile using my pictures.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Section 499 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), does the creation and dissemination of private photographs of an individual by another person, without their consent, and with the intention of causing harm to their reputation, constitute the offence of defamation? 

Furthermore, does the creation of a fake social media profile using the private photographs of another individual, as described, contravene Article 10 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), specifically the provisions related to creating or operating a fake digital identity?

case_description: A shop is openly selling obscene magazines and DVDs to school children near a school campus.
offense_category: sale of obscene material to children
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 226(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is respectfully submitted to seek a legal opinion on whether the sale of obscene materials, as defined under Article 117(5) of BNS, to school children near a school campus constitutes an offence under Article 117(1)(d) of BNS.

Further, under Article 33(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is requested to determine the appropriate procedure for seizure of the obscene materials and the subsequent action to be taken against the shop owner under Article 33(3) of BNSS.

Additionally, under Section 23 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), we seek clarification on the admissibility of evidence in court, specifically with regards to the testimony of school children as witnesses, and the application of Section 24(2)(a) of BSA on the reliability of such evidence.

case_description: A man standing on the road deliberately shows obscene images on his phone to women passing by.
rephrased_query: Under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), whether the act of a man displaying obscene images on his phone to women passing by constitutes an offence under Article 321(1)(a) of BNS, specifically an act intended to outrage the modesty of a woman, and if so, what are the corresponding legal consequences under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the perpetrator, including the provisions for arrest, detention, and trial, as per Section 43(2)(a)(i) of BNSS. Additionally, what are the admissibility and evidentiary requirements under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for proof of the said offence, including the burden of proof and the standard of proof, as per Article 91(3) of BSA.

case_description: A woman was raped by a man who broke into her house late at night when she was alone.
rephrased_query: Whether the act constituting aggravated assault under Article 321(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, committed by the perpetrator who broke into the complainant's residence in contravention of Article 153(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and subsequently engaged in non-consensual sexual conduct with the complainant, constitutes the offence of sexual assault under Article 456(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, and if so, what is the relevant burden of proof and standard of proof to be applied in the trial, as per Article 278 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023.

case_description: A college professor asked a female student for sexual favours in exchange for better grades.
offense_category: sexual harassment and abuse of authority
rephrased_query: Whether the act of a college professor soliciting a female student for sexual favours in exchange for better academic grades falls within the scope of the offence defined under Article 377 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), specifically in relation to 'exploitation of a vulnerable individual', and whether such act would be considered an act of 'coercion' or 'undue influence' under Article 13 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), thus attracting the provisions of the BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023) for 'criminal conspiracy', and what evidence can be adduced to support the prosecution's case under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to establish the guilt of the accused.

case_description: A man has been following a woman from her office to her home daily, sending unwanted gifts, and watching her through binoculars.
rephrased_query:
**Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) Query**

The following incident is reported: A person has been continuously following another individual, a woman, from her place of work to her residence, on multiple occasions. He has also been dispatching unwarranted gifts to her residence. Furthermore, he has been observing her through a pair of binoculars on various instances.

**Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) relevant provisions:**

- Has the perpetrator committed the offence of stalking under Article 234(1)(a) of the BNS, which defines stalking as 'continuously following or attempting to gain access to a person with a view to engaging in non-consensual conduct'?
- Has the accused's actions constituted a 'criminal intimidation' offence under Article 292(2)(a) of the BNS, given the unwarranted gifts and observation through binoculars?
- Are there sufficient grounds to suspect the perpetrator of committing a 'harassment by use of surveillance device' offence under Article 314(1) of the BNS, considering the use of binoculars to observe the woman?
- What preliminary investigation and evidence collection procedures should be undertaken as per Article 43(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to gather evidence and determine the extent of the perpetrator's involvement in the alleged offences?

**Evidence Requirements:**

- What documentary and physical evidence should be collected and preserved, as per Article 18(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), to support or refute the allegations made against the perpetrator?
- Should the victim's statements and testimony be recorded, as per Article 31(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), to document her account of the incidents and provide corroborative evidence?

case_description: A man grabbed a woman's dupatta and tried to disrobe her in a market while others watched.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), an application is sought for the registration of a criminal complaint under offences related to outraging a woman's modesty and assault, as per Article 321, BNS. 

Under what circumstances would a case be made out under BNS Article 321, BNS, and what would be the admissibility of evidence under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in establishing the accused's guilt and the complainant's testimony? Furthermore, what provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) would be applicable in the matter of investigation, trial, and disposal of the complaint, particularly with regard to the duty of the police under BNSS Article 45, and the powers of the Magistrate under BNSS Article 62?

case_description: A married man had sexual intercourse with his wife during judicial separation against her will.
rephrased_query: Whether the act of the married man having sexual intercourse with his wife during the pendency of judicial separation (as per BNS, Article 123) against her will, constitutes an act of sexual assault under BNS, Article 221(1)(d), and if so, whether the said act would be a cognizable offence under BNSS, Article 53(1)(a), and whether the burden of proof would shift to the accused under BSA, Article 21(1), and whether the said act would be considered as rape under BNS, Article 218(1)(b) in view of the absence of her consent.

case_description: A man secretly installed a hidden camera in the women's changing room of a gym to record videos.
rephrased_query:
Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a complaint is sought to be lodged against an individual who allegedly committed the offence of secretly installing a hidden camera in the women's changing room of a gym to record videos, thereby violating Article 23 of the BNS, which prohibits voyeurism and other forms of unwarranted surveillance, and potentially engaging in an act amounting to the offence of stalking or harassment under Article 24 of the BNS.

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the complainant seeks an order for the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Article 42 of the BNSS, and a subsequent investigation be conducted to gather evidence, including the seizure of the hidden camera and any recorded videos, in accordance with the provisions of Sections 156 and 157 of the BNSS.

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the complainant seeks to rely on the provisions of Article 13, which deals with the admissibility of electronic evidence, and Article 20, which pertains to the burden of proof, to establish the guilt of the accused and to secure a conviction under the BNS.

case_description: A man deceived a woman into believing they were lawfully married and cohabited with her for months.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Deception and Cohabitation under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

To the Hon'ble Magistrate of this Court,

Whether the accused, by virtue of Article 17(1) of the BNS, has committed the offence of Deception, as defined under Article 17(2)(a) of the BNS, by inducing the complainant to cohabit with him with the false representation that they were lawfully married?

Whether the complainant's prolonged cohabitation with the accused, subsequent to the deception, constitutes sufficient prima facie evidence to establish the offence of Cohabitation by Deception, as per Article 25(3) of the BNS?

Whether the accused's actions, as alleged by the complainant, amount to an offence punishable under Article 34(1) of the BNS, and thus, warrants an investigation under Section 37(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS)?

Whether the complainant's testimony, as corroborated by material evidence, satisfies the requirements of Section 10(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to establish the alleged offence, and thus, warrants further investigation and proceedings?

Please advise.

case_description: A man who is already married performed a second marriage with another woman without disclosing his first marriage.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), whether the act of a man who has entered into a second marriage without disclosing his existing marital status to the second spouse, constitutes an offence under Article 494 of the BNS, specifically "Marrying again during the lifetime of a husband or wife."

case_description: A woman left her newborn baby in a dustbin near the hospital and disappeared.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a query arises as to whether the act of abandoning a newborn child in a public place, specifically a dustbin near a hospital, constitutes the offence of "Negligent Homicide or Culpable Homicide" under Article 304 of the BNS. Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is pertinent to inquire as to the manner in which the police shall investigate this incident, specifically whether a magisterial inquiry under Section 176 of the BNSS is warranted to determine the cause of death and the circumstances surrounding the abandonment of the newborn child.

Additionally, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), it is necessary to consider the admissibility of evidence in this case, particularly whether the testimony of any witnesses or the medical examination of the newborn child's body shall be admissible under Article 60 of the BSA as relevant to the case.

case_description: A begging ring operator hired several children aged 7-10 to beg at traffic signals and took all the money they collected.
rephrased_query:
Can you please clarify the age range of the children involved in this incident, as your statement mentions 7-10 years, while typically in many jurisdictions, children under 7 are considered minors. Assuming the age range is indeed 7-10, here is a rewritten query based on the new laws:

Whether the actions of the begging ring operator constitute an offence under Article 321 (BNS) - Child Labour, and if so, what provisions of Article 321 (BNS) are applicable to this situation? 

Additionally, what are the obligations of the authorities under Article 234 (BNSS) - Duties of Police Officers, in relation to the welfare and protection of the children involved in this incident? 

Lastly, what evidence, if any, can be relied upon under Article 109 (BSA) - Types of Evidence, to prove the guilt of the begging ring operator, and what is the admissibility of testimony from the children in this regard, especially considering their age and potential vulnerability?

case_description: A couple secretly delivered a baby and disposed of the body to conceal the birth from neighbours.
rephrased_query:
Whether the actions of the couple constitute an offence under the provisions of Section 312, BNS (Abortion not permitted), read with Section 201, BNS (Causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender), and Section 203, BNS (Giving false information respecting an offence committed), in conjunction with Section 34, BNS (Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention).

Further, whether the couple can be held liable under Section 174, BNSS (Police inquest) for concealing the birth and disposing of the body, and if so, what are the consequences of their actions under the provisions of Section 176, BNSS (Magistrate inquest)?

Additionally, whether the prosecution can rely on the circumstantial evidence gathered in this case, and if so, what provisions of the BSA (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023) would be applicable in establishing the guilt of the couple, particularly Section 30, BSA (Burden of proof), and Section 105, BSA (Presumption as to abetment of offence).

case_description: A minor girl aged 14 was procured by a broker and supplied to a client for sexual exploitation.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is respectfully requested to clarify the following legal issue:

Whether, under Article 372(2) of the BNS, the procurement and supply of a minor girl (aged 14) for the purpose of sexual exploitation, perpetrated by a broker and a client, constitutes an offence punishable under Article 456(1) BNS, and if so, what are the consequent penal consequences for the abovementioned accused parties?

Additionally, please provide guidance on the applicability of Article 234 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in admissibility of evidence in respect of the minor girl's age and the procurement and supply of her services for sexual exploitation.

Furthermore, it is requested to clarify the procedural aspects of this case under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), specifically with regard to the requirements of Article 278(1) BNSS for registration of the offence, and the provisions of Article 321(3) BNSS for investigation and gathering of evidence.

case_description: A doctor performed an abortion on a woman in her eighth month of pregnancy without medical justification, and the baby died.
rephrased_query:
Is the doctor liable under Section 316(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for causing the death of the foetus, and if so, can they be prosecuted under Article 173 of the BNSS 2023 for causing death or injury contrary to section 316(1) BNS 2023? 

Furthermore, under Section 53(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), can the prosecution rely on circumstantial evidence to establish the doctor's criminal liability for the death of the foetus, given that they performed the abortion without medical justification?

case_description: A woman was forcibly given medicine by her mother-in-law to cause a miscarriage because the family wanted a boy child.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Section 322 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a formal complaint is lodged against the mother-in-law for alleged commission of the offence of voluntarily causing miscarriage, with the intention of causing the unborn child to be born dead, or of causing the woman to miscarry her unborn child.

Further, under Section 498 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), the husband and other relatives of the accused are also implicated for allegedly subjecting the woman to cruelty, amounting to an offence under this provision.

Additionally, under Article 12 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the investigating officer is directed to take cognizance of the case and initiate an inquiry into the allegations of the offence, as the same appears to be a cognizable offence.

Lastly, under Article 15 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the burden of proof of the accused's intention to cause the miscarriage shall lie on the prosecution, as the accused is presumed to be innocent until proven guilty.

case_description: A 5-year-old child was enticed with chocolates by a neighbour who then kept the child locked in his house for two days.
rephrased_query:
Petition under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for commission of the offence(s) punishable under Article 226 (Kidnapping) and/or Article 245 (False Imprisonment) against the neighbour in question.

Query:
